# Data in BiologyToBioimage: everything is generated by code

The repository stores **no data files and no pictures**. Every image, time-lapse, point pattern
and figure in the 29 notebooks is produced by code that runs inside the notebook. Data come from
the simulators in [`course_toolkit.py`](course_toolkit.py) (copied verbatim into each notebook that
uses them) or from small simulation functions written in the notebook itself.

Why simulate?

- **A known truth.** Every simulator returns the hidden ground truth — the true cell shapes and
  positions, the true association between two channels, the true lineage of a dividing cell, the
  true transform relating two images — so every method can be *checked*: the notebooks contain
  🧪 *ground-truth checks* that a real, unlabelled microscopy image could not provide.
- **A slim, self-contained repository.** Nothing to download, no licences to track, no broken
  links; every notebook runs offline on a free CPU in minutes.
- **Reproducible.** A fixed `SEED` means every notebook (and every student) sees the same data and
  the same numbers.

What simulation cannot teach — the messiness, scale and artefacts of real microscopy data — is
covered in each Level 2 module's 🧭 *From toy to real data* section, which names public tools,
model zoos and landmark data sets to try next. The synthetic images reproduce the *structure* of
real bioimages (blobby or elongated objects, point-spread-function blur, sensor and shot noise,
multiple channels, time); they never claim to reproduce a specific published data set, and the
notebooks say so.

---

## Core simulators (`course_toolkit.py`)

| Simulator | Mimics | What it returns (hidden truth in **bold**) | Modules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `simulate_nuclei_image(...)` | a fluorescence image of cell nuclei/cells (round, elongated, kidney-shaped, …), optionally touching or dividing | the image, **instance mask**, **shape class per cell**, **cell centres/radii** | 00, 02, 05–13, 19–22, 24, 26 |
| `simulate_two_channel_image(...)` | two co-imaged fluorescence channels (e.g. two labelled proteins) with a chosen degree of spatial association | both channel images, **the planted association strength**, **per-spot ground truth** | 05, 18, 21, 28 |
| `simulate_time_lapse(...)` | a time-lapse of moving, occasionally dividing particles or cells | the frame sequence, **per-object trajectories**, **division events/lineage** | 14, 28 |
| `simulate_point_pattern(...)` | a 2-D spatial point pattern (e.g. molecule or cell positions) | the coordinates, **the planted pattern**: random / clustered / dispersed | 05, 18 |
| `simulate_registration_pair(...)` | a "moving" image obtained by applying a known rigid/similarity transform to a reference image | both images, **the true transform** (rotation, translation, scale) | 15 |
| `degrade_image(image, psf_sigma, noise_sigma, seed)` | the forward imaging model: blur by a known point-spread function plus sensor noise | the degraded image, **the true PSF and noise level used to generate it** | 16, 17, 20, 21 |
| `gaussian_psf(sigma, radius)`, `blur_image(image, psf)` | the microscope's optical blur (point-spread function) and convolving an image with it | the PSF kernel / the blurred image | 02, 04, 16, 17 |
| `add_gaussian_noise`, `add_poisson_noise`, `add_salt_pepper_noise`, `add_periodic_noise` | the classic noise sources of a camera sensor: read noise, shot noise, impulse noise, scan-line pickup | the noisy image (clean image kept for comparison) | 02, 16 |

## Worked-example tables (toolkit constants)

| Constant | What it is | Modules |
|---|---|---|
| `SHAPE_CLASSES` | the fixed set of synthetic nucleus/cell shape classes (`_draw_blob` draws one) used throughout the course as the classification/segmentation/tracking target | 05, 07–13, 19–22, 24, 26 |
| `SOBEL_X`, `SOBEL_Y` | the literal 3×3 Sobel gradient kernels | 06 |

## Simulators written locally in a single notebook

Several modules — mostly in Level 2, where no one shared simulator fits every research area —
define a small, documented simulator of their own rather than adding it to the shared toolkit (the
rule in *Rules for contributors* below explains why):

| Local simulator (where it is defined) | Mimics | Hidden truth |
|---|---|---|
| In-/out-of-distribution shape-mix evaluation sets (Module 20) | a held-out shape mixture the model was not tuned on, to compare a specialist U-Net against a training-free generalist segmenter | **which shapes are in- vs. out-of-distribution** |
| Paired label-free/"stained" channel pairs (Module 21) | a low-contrast, blurred "label-free" view paired with a crisp "ground-truth stain" view of the same cells | **the true stain intensity the model must predict, and when it is forced to hallucinate** |
| Per-treatment cell populations with an injected batch effect (Module 22) | a high-content screen across simulated treatments and plates/batches | **the true treatment effect**, separated from **the injected, purely technical batch effect** |
| A multiplexed, multi-marker synthetic tissue (Module 23) | several co-imaged marker channels defining a handful of synthetic cell types arranged with planted spatial structure | **per-cell type**, **the planted spatial neighbourhood structure/niches** |
| A calibration/active-learning classifier pool (Module 24) | a pool of labelled and unlabelled synthetic cells for calibration and active-learning experiments | **the true label of every pool image**, used only for evaluation, never for training before it is "labelled" |
| A small 3-D nuclei volume (Module 25) | a multi-plane, correlated-in-z extension of the 2-D nucleus simulator | **the full-volume 3-D instance mask** |
| An out-of-distribution test set and a leaky vs. grouped train/test split (Module 26) | the two most common ways a bioimage model silently fails: distribution shift and data leakage | **which split is leaky**, **which test images are out of distribution** |
| A toy model-zoo registry and a synthetic text corpus (Module 27) | a BioImage.IO-style registry of tools an agent can call, and a small corpus for a retrieval demo | **the correct tool/answer for each query**, used to check the agent's and the retriever's output |

These are documented where they are defined, follow the same SIMULATED-labelling and
ground-truth-return conventions as the shared toolkit, and reuse the shared toolkit's simulators as
their building blocks wherever that is natural (for example, several extend `simulate_nuclei_image`
rather than drawing cells from scratch).

---

## Rules for contributors

- Do not add data files, pictures, downloads or file reads. The validator
  (`python validate_notebooks.py`) rejects stored data files, files over 400 kB, embedded or linked
  pictures (the Colab badge is the only external image), and code that downloads or reads data.
- Generate data with the toolkit or with a documented simulation function in the notebook; return
  the hidden truth and use it in a 🧪 ground-truth check.
- Label simulated data (print a line noting it is simulated, put "SIMULATED" in plot titles where
  natural) and explain what the simulation mimics and what it cannot teach.
- If a new simulator is useful to several notebooks, add it to `course_toolkit.py`, then replace the
  copy in the 🧰 toolkit cell of every notebook that uses it — the validator reports copies that
  differ from the reference file.
